<h2>SherlockEQ 0.3.2</h2>

<p>
  This release adds a command-line interface. <code>sherlockeq</code> is a
  power-user and automation surface for the app — check status, switch
  profiles, toggle Reference Mode, nudge gain, balance, and the simple EQ,
  list output devices, import or export profiles, and dump diagnostics for a
  bug report. The running app stays in charge: the CLI just asks it to report
  or change state, so anything you do on the command line shows up in the
  window and the menu bar right away.
</p>

<h3>Added</h3>

<ul>
  <li>
    <strong>The <code>sherlockeq</code> command-line tool.</strong>
    <code>sherlockeq status</code> for a one-glance summary;
    <code>profiles list / active / activate / import / export</code>;
    <code>bypass on|off|toggle</code>; <code>gain</code>, <code>balance</code>,
    and <code>simple-eq</code> get/set; <code>devices list / current</code>;
    <code>diagnostics</code> for a structured snapshot to attach to a bug
    report; plus <code>launch</code> and <code>quit</code>. Most commands take
    <code>--json</code> for scripting, return meaningful exit codes, and fail
    cleanly with a clear message when the app isn't running. Everything is
    local — no telemetry, no network.
  </li>
  <li>
    <strong>It installs with the app.</strong>
    Homebrew (<code>brew install --cask sherlockeq</code>) now puts
    <code>sherlockeq</code> on your PATH automatically. If you installed the
    app directly, the tool ships inside the bundle — run
    <code>"/Applications/SherlockEQ.app/Contents/Helpers/sherlockeq" install</code>
    once to symlink it onto your PATH.
  </li>
</ul>

<h3>Not a medical device</h3>

<p>
  SherlockEQ is not a healthcare or medical application. It does not diagnose,
  treat, measure, or monitor any hearing condition, tinnitus, or disability.
  For concerns about your hearing, consult a doctor, audiologist, or licensed
  healthcare professional.
</p>
